title: Replace make audit's dead literal-phrase TODO/FIXME/XXX grep with a real AG-6 check
rule: AG-6 (every TODO/FIXME carries a Linear DNI-#### id) / Rule 0

evidence.quote: if grep -rn "TODO: refactor later\|FIXME: hardcoded for now\|XXX: temporary" lib/ --include="*.dart" | grep -q .; then \
// TODO: Add more integration tests as features are implemented:

why: Audit check 10/15 ('No banned TODO/FIXME/XXX markers') matches only three exact, oddly-specific literal phrases. Verified: `grep -rn "TODO: refactor later\|FIXME: hardcoded for now\|XXX: temporary" learning_tracker/lib/` returns zero hits anywhere in the app, and always will — no developer writes that literal string. Meanwhile there are real, uncaught TODOs with no Linear id anywhere (`grep -c "DNI-[0-9]"` on all lib/ TODO/FIXME lines returns 0 of 4), and my own batch contains a live example the check silently misses: integration_test/app_test.dart:25. This grep gives the false impression that TODO/FIXME hygiene (AG-6) is enforced by `make audit`, when in fact it enforces nothing a real comment would ever trip.
recommendation: Change the pattern to match any `// TODO`/`// FIXME`/`// XXX` NOT followed by `DNI-\d+` (e.g. `grep -rnE '//\s*(TODO|FIXME|XXX)' lib/ | grep -vE 'DNI-[0-9]+'`), which is what AG-6 actually requires.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` fails on any TODO/FIXME/XXX comment in lib/ (or test/) lacking a DNI-#### id.
A regression fixture (one TODO with a DNI id, one without) proves the new grep distinguishes them.
